findings.name: Pre-ticked consent
findings.evidence: Send me Leafbox offers and share my details with partners
findings.why: Consent you didn't give is not consent. Pre-ticked boxes quietly sign people up for marketing or data sharing they never chose.
findings.fix: Leave every consent checkbox unticked by default and let people opt in.

findings.name: Sneak into basket
findings.why: Paid extras that are pre-selected end up in the basket unless the shopper notices and removes them.
findings.fix: Offer extras unticked; only add them to the order after an explicit choice.

findings.name: Hidden subscription terms
findings.evidence: Your membership renews automatically at $89.99/month after the 7-day trial until cancelled. To cancel, you must call our member services line during business h…
findings.why: Burying auto-renewal or post-trial charges in fine print turns a 'free trial' into a subscription people didn't knowingly agree to.
findings.fix: State the price, billing frequency and renewal date clearly next to the sign-up button, at the same size as the offer.
refs: California Automatic Renewal Law, Bus. & Prof. Code §17600 et seq.

findings.name: Asymmetric consent
findings.evidence: 'Accept all' offered with no equally easy way to refuse
findings.why: When 'Accept' is one bright click and 'Reject' is hidden, tiny or missing, the banner manufactures consent rather than asking for it.
findings.fix: Put 'Reject all' on the first layer, with the same size, style and number of clicks as 'Accept all'.

findings.name: False urgency
findings.why: Countdown timers and 'ends soon' banners pressure people into deciding before they can compare or think. They are often fake and reset on reload.
findings.fix: Only show deadlines that are real, and state the actual end date.
refs: EU Unfair Commercial Practices Directive, Annex I point 7
FTC, Bringing Dark Patterns to Light (2022)

findings.name: Drip pricing
findings.why: Advertising a low price and revealing mandatory fees later makes honest comparison impossible and exploits sunk-cost at checkout.
findings.fix: Show the total price, including mandatory fees, wherever a price is shown.
refs: FTC Rule on Unfair or Deceptive Fees, 16 CFR Part 464 (2025)

findings.name: Trick question
findings.evidence: Uncheck this box if you do not want to not receive SMS updates
findings.why: Double negatives and inverted checkboxes ('untick to not receive') make people choose the opposite of what they intend.
findings.fix: Phrase every option positively: 'Send me offers by email' with an unticked box.
refs: FTC, Bringing Dark Patterns to Light (2022)

findings.name: Confirmshaming
findings.evidence: No thanks, I prefer paying full price for sad food
findings.why: Wording the 'no' option as a self-insult guilts people into accepting.
findings.fix: Use neutral labels for every choice, e.g. 'No thanks'.
refs: FTC, Bringing Dark Patterns to Light (2022)

findings.name: Obstructed cancellation
findings.evidence: Your membership renews automatically at $89.99/month after the 7-day trial until cancelled. To cancel, you must call our member services line during business h…
findings.why: Easy to join, hard to leave: forcing a phone call or letter to cancel keeps people paying for things they no longer want.
findings.fix: Let people cancel the same way they signed up, online, in a few clicks.
refs: California Automatic Renewal Law, Bus. & Prof. Code §17602

findings.name: Activity notifications
findings.evidence: Priya in Austin just bought the Family Plan
findings.why: Pop-ups like 'Sarah in Leeds just bought this' simulate popularity and are frequently fabricated.
findings.fix: Remove simulated activity feeds; if you show real activity, make it verifiable and aggregate.
refs: EU Unfair Commercial Practices Directive, Art. 6 (misleading actions)
Mathur et al., Dark Patterns at Scale (2019)

findings.name: Scarcity pressure
findings.evidence: Only 3 left at this price · 14 people are viewing this right now
findings.why: Low-stock and high-demand messages push people to buy now. They are legal when true, but often generated without real inventory data.
findings.fix: Show stock levels only when they come from live inventory, and avoid manufactured 'people are looking' counters.
refs: EU Unfair Commercial Practices Directive, Art. 6
Mathur et al., Dark Patterns at Scale (2019)
